articles.title: Fulham's Rodrigo Muniz speaks about wife's miscarriage during 'difficult' season
articles.summary: Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz, who scored for his side in a 1-1 draw against Newcastle United, speaks of the struggles he endured last season.
articles.body:
Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz has spoken of the struggles he endured last season, revealing his wife suffered a miscarriage.

Muniz scored the equaliser for the Cottagers in a 1-1 draw against Newcastle United on Saturday for his first league goal since their opening top-flight match of last season.

"Last season was really difficult for me because, now I can say it, but I had the surgery," said the 25-year-old Brazilian, who had an operation on a hamstring injury , external in November and was out until early February.

"My wife was pregnant last season and, unfortunately, we lost the baby, but God is good all the time and now she's pregnant again.

"The goal was for my baby, and I hope this season will be different than last season."

Muniz also scored in wins over AFC Wimbledon and West Ham in the Carabao Cup this season.

Overall, he has 19 goals and three assists in 86 Premier League appearances for the London club since joining from Flamengo in 2021.

"I train hard every week to get opportunities to play and I want to play more," said Muniz, whose eight Premier League appearances under manager Alvaro Arbeloa this season have all come off the bench.

"I cannot control the gaffer, but I showed the gaffer I want to play more. I have to keep training hard, for him to say, 'OK, now is your time', and then I'm ready."

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo receives tributes from every former club and league he played for, except one that owes him most: Real Madrid
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement from international football is met with heartfelt tributes from former clubs and leagues apart from Real Madrid, highlighting his incredible career and achievements in football.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement from international football has prompted tributes from the clubs where he made his name, the leagues in which he dominated and the organisations that have witnessed his record-breaking career. Yet one notable absence has drawn attention. Real Madrid, the club where he became its greatest goalscorer and won four Champions League titles, has offered no public acknowledgement of his departure from Portugal.Real Madrid's silence stands out after Ronaldo's Portugal retirementManchester United, Sporting CP, Juventus and Al Nassr have all publicly recognised Ronaldo following his announcement that he would no longer represent Portugal. Messages have also come from the Premier League, Liga Portugal, the Saudi Pro League, UEFA and FIFA, with each acknowledging the extraordinary international career of a player who scored 146 goals in 234 appearances for his country.Real Madrid, however, has not issued a statement or published a tribute on its official social media accounts or website, according to reports published after Ronaldo's announcement on November 5. The absence is particularly striking given the significance of his nine seasons in the Spanish capital, where he established himself as the club's all-time leading goalscorer.Ronaldo joined Madrid from Manchester United in 2009 and remained until 2018, scoring 450 goals in 438 official appearances. He won four Champions League titles, two La Liga championships and a collection of domestic and international trophies, becoming the central figure in one of the most successful periods in the club's modern history.The silence does not, by itself, establish any disagreement between the player and his former club, nor has Real Madrid explained why it has not issued a message. But the contrast with the responses from his other former employers has made the omission difficult to overlook.Ronaldo's nine years at Real Madrid produced a historic legacyRonaldo arrived at the Santiago Bernabéu in the summer of 2009 after Manchester United accepted a then-world-record transfer fee of £80 million. He had already won the Premier League, Champions League and his first Ballon d'Or at Old Trafford, but his move to Spain took his career into a different dimension.Across 438 official appearances, he scored 450 goals, making him Real Madrid's record scorer despite spending fewer than a decade at the club. His tally placed him ahead of Karim Benzema, who finished his Madrid career with 354 goals, and established a standard that has remained central to discussions of the club's greatest players.His trophy collection included four Champions League titles, two La Liga championships, two Copa del Rey trophies, two Spanish Super Cups, three UEFA Super Cups and three FIFA Club World Cups. He was also awarded four Ballon d'Or titles during his Madrid years, in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017, adding to the first he had won at Manchester United.His individual records were equally significant. Ronaldo scored 17 goals during the 2013-14 Champions League campaign, setting a competition record for a single season, and registered 34 hat-tricks in La Liga. He was the leading scorer in the Champions League in each of Madrid's four title-winning campaigns between 2014 and 2018.The relationship ended in July 2018, when Ronaldo joined Juventus after nine seasons in Spain. His departure came after he had helped Madrid win three consecutive Champions League titles between 2016 and 2018, a period in which the club re-established itself as the dominant force in European football.Sporting, Manchester United and Juventus lead the club tributesSporting CP, where Ronaldo began his senior professional career, was among the first clubs to acknowledge his international retirement. The Portuguese club posted: "Thank you for everything you did for our Nation. Forever in the history of Portugal."Ronaldo came through Sporting's academy before making his senior debut during the 2002-03 season. His performances attracted Manchester United, who signed him as an 18-year-old in 2003. The move began a six-year first spell at Old Trafford in which he scored 118 goals and won three consecutive Premier League titles, an FA Cup, two League Cups, the Community Shield, the FIFA Club World Cup and the Champions League in 2008. He also won his first Ballon d'Or that year.United welcomed his international retirement with a message that read: "Congratulations on an incredible international career, Cristiano. Enjoy your retirement." The club accompanied the post with a goat image, a reference to the widely used 'greatest of all time' description.Ronaldo returned to Old Trafford in 2021 for a second spell, scoring another 27 goals before leaving in November 2022. His two periods at United produced 145 goals in total and established a connection with the club that extended well beyond his first arrival as a teenager.Juventus also paid tribute to the Portuguese forward, posting: "Congratulations on an incredible journey with Portugal, Cristiano."Ronaldo spent three seasons in Turin after leaving Madrid in 2018, scoring 101 goals and winning two Serie A titles, the Coppa Italia and two Supercoppa Italiana trophies. His time in Italy added another major domestic league to a career that had already brought success in England and Spain.Al Nassr, where Ronaldo continues his club career, offered a more extensive tribute. The Saudi club described him as an inspiration to generations and recognised the legacy he had created for Portugal, while making clear that his departure from international football would not end his story in Riyadh."An inspiration to generations… and an extraordinary sporting legacy. He has bid farewell to Portugal, but will remain in the hearts of people all over the world. One chapter has come to an end… but a new story is yet to be written with his club, Al-Nassr," the club wrote.A separate message focused on the relationship between Ronaldo, the supporters and the city, declaring that there were still chapters to be written together. The club's response was a reminder that, although his Portugal career has ended, his playing career continues in the Saudi Pro League.Premier League, Liga Portugal and Saudi Pro League join the tributesThe response extended beyond the clubs that employed Ronaldo. Liga Portugal, the competition in which he first played senior football, published two messages recognising his contribution to Portuguese football and his influence around the world."You’ve written a golden chapter in Portuguese football. Thank you for everything, Cristiano," one post read. Another described how he had carried the Portuguese flag across the world, thanking him as captain.The Premier League also acknowledged his international career, posting: "Congratulations on a historic international career, @cristiano."Ronaldo's achievements in England included three consecutive league titles with Manchester United between 2007 and 2009, alongside the Champions League triumph in 2008. His return to the club in 2021 brought him back to the competition where he had first established himself as one of the world's leading players.Portugal, UEFA and FIFA recognise a record-breaking international careerThe most significant tributes came from the organisations responsible for Portugal and international football. The Portuguese Football Federation issued a statement expressing "profound gratitude and immense admiration" for Ronaldo's service to the country, recognising his leadership, dedication and influence on generations of young players.The federation described him as a symbol of the national team's spirit and highlighted the 234 appearances and 146 goals that made him the leading appearance-maker and goalscorer in men's international football. It also made clear that his departure would not pass without a formal farewell, saying it intended to organise a tribute at which supporters and the country could celebrate his career.Portugal's official national-team account shared a retrospective video accompanied by the message: "A story that will live on forever. Obrigado por tudo, Capitão." Another post reduced his international career to three figures: "Matches: 234. Goals: 146. Legacy: ∞."UEFA highlighted the trophies that defined Ronaldo's time with Portugal, acknowledging his European Championship triumph in 2016 and the Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025."What an international career! One EURO title, two UEFA Nations League titles and a legacy that will last forever. Thank you, @Cristiano!" the governing body wrote.FIFA's tribute focused on another of his achievements: becoming the first player to score at six different editions of the men's World Cup. Ronaldo appeared at every tournament from 2006 to 2026, extending a record that reflects the extraordinary longevity of his international career."The first player to score goals in six different editions of the @FIFAWorldCup. Congratulations on an incredible international career, @Cristiano!" the official FIFA World Cup account posted.Ronaldo's international journey began on August 20, 2003, against Kazakhstan and ended with a 1-0 victory over Wales on September 24, 2026. In between, he captained Portugal to its first European Championship, two Nations League titles and a succession of records that have made him the most prolific goalscorer in men's international football.His own farewell message was brief: "Portugal will always be in my heart." The response from his former clubs, leagues and football's governing bodies showed how far that career had travelled. articles.summary: Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman wanted his players to savor Saturday's 31-24 victory over top-ranked Miami.
articles.body:
Notre Dame coach Marcus Freeman wanted his players to savor Saturday's 31-24 victory over top-ranked Miami.

Freeman called the upset a "special moment." While he's still focused on the larger goals, he understands the significance of taking down the Hurricanes.

"This is big, this is special," he told reporters . "I'm not going to sit here and say this is like the other ones. No, this is different. There was a lot of emotion, a lot of physical preparation, mental preparation, we put into this. I want them to enjoy it."

The Fighting Irish jumped ahead 24-3 in the third quarter before Miami attempted its comeback. The Hurricanes twice cut the deficit to one score but couldn't erase Notre Dame's lead.

The result will have had Heisman Trophy implications .

Fighting Irish quarterback CJ Carr went 29-of-40 for 319 yards and three touchdowns, while Miami's Darian Mensah was 24-of-43 for 276 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. Carr is the Heisman betting favorite (+150) at FanDuel Sportsbook .

The College Football Playoff selection committee will eventually have its say as well.

Notre Dame being ranked 11th despite having a 7-1 record was one of the more contentious choices by the CFP voters. Now, the team figures to make a big jump.

"We learned that last year, it doesn't matter what you're ranked until the last week, and that's the truth," Freeman said. "We don't need to focus on it. We don't need to talk about it. Our job was to leave no doubt today, and they [did not]."

Of course, Saturday's win will be irrelevant if Notre Dame stumbles before the finish line. The Fighting Irish have Boston College, SMU and Syracuse the rest of the way.

articles.title: Wrexham news: Shock changes and vital results - the Red Dragons' seismic week
articles.summary: BBC Sport Wales addresses the key changes made at Wrexham in what was a seismic week for the Championship club.
articles.body:
In the midst of a pivotal week for Wrexham , the club announced a shock shake-up within the boardroom.

Gone was chief executive officer Michael Williamson, back came director Shaun Harvey as acting CEO.

While change occurred off the pitch, Phil Parkinson steadied the ship on it.

Watching over were co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, who were in attendance for the 1-1 draw with Wolverhampton Wanderers, , which came just shy of 24 hours after Williamson's exit.

Make no mistake, as Wrexham bid to achieve more success under their star owners, there is no doubt that recent changes at the Racecourse Ground have been immensely significant.

From afar, Williamson's exit came as a surprise.

Williamson was appointed to the role of CEO just 34 days after Wrexham sealed promotion - at the time their second under Parkinson - into League One by thumping Forest Green Rovers 6-0 in north Wales.

The American - who previously worked at clubs including Inter Milan, DC United and Miami FC - oversaw huge growth as Wrexham evolved during their rise.

Overall staff numbers increased from 255 to 313 in his first year at the club, while Wrexham's iconic Racecourse Ground is also expanding.

Williamson had been a key figure in the development of Wrexham's new £69m Kop Stand, which is due to be completed next year.

He oversaw what was Wrexham's third successive promotion into the Championship - where the Red Dragons earned a highest-ever finish of seventh in 2025-26.

In November 2025, Williamson was named Football Industry Leader of the Year at the inaugural Global Football Industry Awards.

The club lauded Williamson for his pivotal role in the creation of the new academy facility at Darland High School, along with the subsequent approval of their English Football League (EFL) academy category three license.

The finances have continued to be boosted too.

Wrexham are expected to report a turnover of between £46m and £50m for the year ending June 2026, a huge jump on the £33.3m club record posted for their 2024-25 League One season , Williamson's first in north Wales.

But there has been growing discontent behind-the-scenes of late.

Wrexham claim point against in-form Wolves

Wrexham owners' presence uplifting - Parkinson

Growing concerns, with community at the heart

Wrexham made a key alteration to their transfer set-up in the summer.

Williamson took a prominent role in the club's transfer operations as director Harvey stepped down from day-to-day operations in early July.

Earlier this season, former Newcastle United chief Steve Nickson was appointed to the newly-created role of sporting director, a move welcomed by boss Parkinson . That said, he did not begin the role until after the summer window.

The transfer market proved difficult, as evidenced by the fact Wrexham were the last of the 24 Championship clubs to make a signing in the summer.

Two of their seven senior recruits - Callum O'Hare and Joe Worrall - joined on deadline day.

Only Danny Imray and Ben Whiteman arrived prior to the season opener against Middlesbrough in the League Cup on 7 August.

They were recently the subject of a bombshell announcement from the EFL regarding the registrations of summer signings O'Hare and Issa Kabore.

The club was fined £75,000 - of which £25,000 was suspended - after the EFL ruled that Kabore and O'Hare were ineligible to feature against Birmingham City and Millwall respectively earlier this season.

It led to the embarrassing situation of Southampton - who Wrexham mocked in the aftermath of the Spygate scandal - poking fun at the Red Dragons when they announced their line-up for the Sheffield United fixture in late October.

It was a game Wrexham went on to lose 1-0 following a lacklustre display, which led to Parkinson raising concerns over the performance of his players.

In the aftermath of the debacle, it was made clear the club want to recruit a new secretary - a vacancy that has existed since current club historian Geraint Parry stepped down from the role a year ago .

But the issues weren't simply behind-the-scenes. There have also been some concerns that the club has shown signs of losing its connection with supporters.

Changes to ticket policies in addition to the £10 surcharge - which was later scrapped due to a backlash from fans - required for supporters to use the Fanzone behind the temporary Kop stand in Williamson's first season at the club left the Wrexham faithful angered.

The club were also criticised in the summer for advertising merchandise featuring a white dragon, typically associated with England as opposed to the red dragon that features on the national flag of Wales.

It was seen as further evidence that the club's strong bond with those who have followed Wrexham through thick and thin has waned.

One beloved figure connected to the Red Dragons even told BBC Sport Wales that the achievements of some of the key members involved in Wrexham's rise have not been sufficiently recognised by some at the club.

In a 139-word statement issued by Mac and Reynolds announcing Williamson's exit, the Hollywood pair wrote: "We remain focused on our most important task: to make the Wrexham community proud."

The word community was twice used in the brief statement. Plenty have made their own interpretations of the words chosen.

The announcement undoubtedly came out of the blue, with many staff on the ground in Wrexham only being made aware of the news shortly before the club's official announcement.

Parkinson himself was only informed on Friday morning prior to his pre-Wolves press conference, held at the club's Colliers Park training ground in the afternoon.

It was perhaps telling that Williamson's usual notes to fans were included in the Wolves matchday programme, despite his exit from the club a day earlier.

Only three days earlier, ahead of an impressive 2-0 victory against Middlesbrough, Williamson had utilised his programme notes to address the fiasco of Wrexham's breaches of player eligibility rules, incidents that occurred prior to sporting director Nickson's arrival.

"We co-operated with the EFL, carried out an internal review and have already taken steps to strengthen our processes and help prevent a recurrence," he wrote.

"As Wrexham AFC grows, our operations and infrastructure must keep pace with our ambitions on the pitch.

"Growth brings responsibility. We are proud of the progress being made, but we must be open and accountable when we fall short of our own standards. That is how we learn and build a stronger club for the long term."

Wrexham have largely operated in an efficient but ruthless fashion since being taken over by Reynolds and Mac in February 2021.

Icons including Paul Mullin, Elliot Lee, Andy Cannon, James McClean, Steven Fletcher and Ollie Palmer have all been moved on during the club's surge up the football pyramid.

Parkinson himself has been the recipient of some criticism during various stages of his five-and-a-half year tenure as boss.

The experienced manager rewarded the faith shown in him this week as his side collected four points in fixtures against two sides in Wolves and Boro that will likely be automatic promotion contenders come the latter stages of the campaign.

Williamson has not been as fortunate, and some of the reaction to his departure spoke volumes.

Former players Mullin, Lee, Cannon and Anthony Forde, along with Humphrey Ker - who recently stepped down as a director after five years with the club - were among those who liked a BBC Sport Wales post confirming Williamson's exit.

When one fan commented that those likes "says it all", former England midfielder Rob Lee - father of ex- Wrexham midfielder Elliot Lee - responded: "Yes it does."

In Harvey, Wrexham feel they have someone who is more than just a safe pair of hands.

The 56-year-old has extensive knowledge of both the Welsh club and the English football structure following previous roles with Leeds United and Bradford City. He was also chief executive of the EFL between 2013 and 2019.

It is a huge part of the reason he has acted as an advisor to Reynolds and Mac ever since the duo became involved in the club.

Following his side's draw with Wolves, Parkinson said: "I had a brief chat with Shaun Harvey this morning.

"Shaun is back in a more official capacity, but he's always been around, he's been here since day one.

"He's an important figure. He understands everything about the club because he was one of the key people in starting off this journey with the owners."

There is clearly a strong bond between those at Wrexham and Harvey.

In the second minute of the contest with Wolves, Harvey headed to his seat in the Racecourse Ground's Macron Stand, known as the Mold Road Stand - the same stand in which Reynolds and Mac are situated for home games - and was roundly applauded by home fans.

The hope is that supporters will be continue to be applauding over the remaining months of the campaign.

Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views

Mac and Reynolds themselves stated Harvey has been an "integral part" of the club's journey.

Harvey could potentially land the role on a permanent basis, although an appointment would require approval from the Independent Football Regulator.

Nevertheless, it proved to be a seismic week for Wrexham.

The two-week international window will give those at the club a chance to take stock.

But the Championship grind will soon kick back in as Wrexham aim to build on their encouraging week on the field and continue their quest to clinch a play-off spot in just shy of six months' time.

"There's togetherness in the stands and with the boys on the pitch - but more than anything, there's just something about this place," the Deadpool star wrote on Instagram after the Wolves draw.

"Some of the best days of my life have been spent in this stadium, standing next to Rob Mac. Today was one of them. Up the Town."

articles.title: 'Bulls--t,' Cristobal Rips Refs for Controversial Decision in Miami's Loss to Notre Dame
articles.summary: After Miami benefited from some contentious officiating decisions earlier this year, the shoe was on the other foot Saturday night.
articles.body:
After Miami benefited from some contentious officiating decisions earlier this year, the shoe was on the other foot Saturday night.

A potential game-tying touchdown catch by Hurricanes tight end Elija Lofton was ruled incomplete in the fourth quarter.

Miami coach Mario Cristobal told reporters he was "really, really disappointed" with the call.

"I'm pissed off. It's bulls--t, and I'll leave it at that," he said. "That's the way it was seen by them. So I got to live with it and respect it, and our players got to live with it, and we got to do better. Again, don't leave it in the hands of the officials."

When it comes to the rulebook, few things can be more maddening in football that determining what is and isn't a catch.

Lofton had two feet land inbounds and control as he came down. It wasn't until he was out of bounds that Notre Dame safety Luke Talich dislodged the ball.

Under the letter of the law , a player needs to "[maintain] control of the ball long enough to enable that player to perform an act common to the game." Defining "an act common to the game" is where the interpretation comes into play.

In the eyes of the officiating crew Saturday night, Lofton clearly didn't satisfy that criteria.

Cristobal and Miami quarterback Darian Mensah conceded a team can't put itself in a position where any one officiating call can influence the outcome.

The Hurricanes fell behind 24-3 in the second half. They didn't find their groove until midway through the third quarter. If they don't dig themselves into such a deep hole, they might be 9-0 right now.

Beyond that, there's no reason for Miami to dwell on this result when its trajectory is basically the same. The team is assured of making the College Football Playoff by winning out and claiming an ACC title.

Maybe the Notre Dame loss is the difference between having a bye to the quarterfinals and hosting a first-round game. But the Canes still control their overall destiny.

articles.title: Michael Vick Reacts to Shocking Loss on Video as NSU Loses in Surprising Way to NC Central
articles.summary: It seemed as if Norfolk State was going to get its first MEAC win of the season under head coach Michael Vick on Saturday.
articles.body:
It seemed as if Norfolk State was going to get its first MEAC win of the season under head coach Michael Vick on Saturday.

The Spartans were well on their way to victory when they recovered a North Carolina Central fumble with the lead and 1:36 left to play, but quarterback David Bailey then lost a fumble as the team ran plays instead of kneeling. NC Central made Vick's team pay with a go-ahead touchdown pass with 27 seconds left before Marco Peery missed a 37-yard field goal attempt that would have won it on the final possession.

"I'm sorry, man," Vick told his team in a video he posted and then deleted after the stunning loss (h/t Antonio Morales of The Athletic). "We've got to help y'all just as much as we ask y'all to help us. There (isn't) too much else to say, fellas. We've got to soak this one in. Great effort. Played your asses off. … I thought it was over, man. Took my headset off. Thought it was over. We were supposed to be in victory (formation)."

While kneeldowns wouldn't have run the entire clock out since NC Central had one timeout remaining, it would have used all but the final seconds.

For his part, Vick told reporters he wanted his team to kneel in that situation.

"I put my headset down, I called victory formation and all we had to do was take a knee and kneel the clock out," Vick said (h/t Morales). "That's just situational football. I don't know what happened in regard to that. I looked up and we were running the ball, then I saw he fumbled. My final instructions were victory formation. That's when you kneel it out. That's when you have zero timeouts left and they had, I think, zero timeouts and the game was over, practically."

It was the type of loss that can undercut the momentum the program has built at times this season.

The 2025 campaign was Vick's first as head coach, and the Spartans went 1-11 without a conference win.

However, they went 4-3 in nonconference play this season and entered MEAC play looking much improved in Vick's second season. While they lost their first two conference games, one of them was by just three points to Delaware State.

Saturday was a chance to get that elusive conference win, but it slipped away in shocking fashion at the end.

Next up is an opportunity against Morgan State, which is also winless in the league, but Saturday's loss will surely take some time to get over.

articles.title: Top Heisman Candidates to Watch in the 2026 Race After Week 10
articles.summary: The 2026 Heisman Trophy race experienced a significant shift in the last week.
articles.body:
The 2026 Heisman Trophy race experienced a significant shift in the last week.

Notre Dame Fighting Irish quarterback C.J. Carr took over the favorite title after his win over Darian Mensah and the Miami Hurricanes.

Mensah's top target, Malachi Toney, was ruled out for a few weeks with an ankle injury. That took the star wide receiver out of the Heisman discussion.

Jeremiah Smith's Heisman stock took another hit in Week 10 due to the Ohio State Buckeyes' third loss of the regular season.

Smith is still in the running for the Heisman because of his incredible statistics, but he sits in a tougher spot to win than he did a few weeks ago.

C.J. Carr is now the Heisman Trophy favorite at FanDuel Sportsbook.

The Notre Dame quarterback threw for 319 yards and three touchdowns in the Irish's win over top-ranked Miami.

Carr has 2,168 passing yards, 21 passing touchdowns and a single interception on the season.

Carr should put up strong numbers in the next three weeks against a trio of unranked teams.

He won't play in any more marquee matchups, but Carr can make a strong closing argument in a Heisman field that changed with Toney's injury and Ohio State's team struggles.

Darian Mensah is still very much in the Heisman conversation despite his head-to-head loss to Carr.

The Miami quarterback ranks second in the FBS in touchdown passes and seventh in the FBS in passing yards.

Mensah put up 276 yards and three touchdowns in Saturday's defeat. He played the Hurricanes back into the contest in the second half after a brutal start.

Just like Carr, Mensah has three unranked opponents in front of him to finish off the regular season.

If he keeps at his current pace, Mensah will remain inside the top 10 in both passing yards and touchdowns.

At minimum, Mensah has earned a trip to New York as a Heisman finalist.

In order to win, Mensah needs to put up big numbers and have Notre Dame unexpectedly slip up so that Carr's stock drops.

Ohio State hasn't had the season it was expected to have, but Jeremiah Smith has put up eye-popping numbers.

Smith is tied for first in touchdown catches, second in receiving yards and fourth in receptions in the FBS.

Smith is arguably the best individual talent in college football, but he has fallen behind Carr and Mensah in the Heisman discussion.

Jayden Daniels in 2023 won the Heisman on a three-loss LSU team and Travis Hunter's Colorado team had four losses in 2024, so there is recent precedent for Smith to win despite OSU's record.

The concern with Ohio State is that its play won't get better with backup quarterback Luke Fahey running the offense. There's a real chance the Buckeyes could finish with four or five losses.

Fahey's overall play hasn't been great, but he's still found a way to get the ball to Smith, who has had 216 yards and two touchdowns in the last two games.

You never know which way the college football season will turn, so as long as Smith is putting up big numbers, he's got a chance to challenge Carr and Mensah for first-place votes.

articles.title: WSL: Liverpool 1-2 Arsenal, Aston Villa 0-1 Man Utd – Alessia Russo double inspires Gunners as Julia Zigiotti Olme earns late United win
articles.summary: WSL round-up as Arsenal beat Liverpool 2-1 thanks to an Alessia Russo double, while Manchester United left it late to claim a 1-0 victory at Aston Villa, with Julia Zigiotti Olme scoring the decisive goal in the second half.
articles.body:
Russo was the difference for Arsenal, opening the scoring after just eight minutes with a composed finish after being picked out by Emily Fox . Liverpool hit back seven minutes later through Beata Olsson , who got away from Leah Williamson before finding the net to bring the hosts level.

But Russo had the final say before the break, arriving at the back post to head home Lisa Baum's delivery and restore Arsenal's lead.

There were chances for Arsenal to extend the lead after the break, with Russo coming agonisingly close to completing her hat-trick. Liverpool weren't giving up, though, and had a big opportunity to snatch a point late on when Cornelia Kapocs couldn't quite connect with a dangerous ball into the box.

The visitors held on, with Russo deservedly named player of the match after another impressive afternoon in front of goal.

Over at Aston Villa , Manchester United had to be patient before finally finding a breakthrough in the second half.

United had plenty of the ball before the break, registering 12 shots and enjoying 66 per cent possession, but couldn't find a way past Villa goalkeeper Akane Okuma .

The hosts came into the game more after half-time and almost made United pay for their missed chances, with Jean-Francois forcing a superb save from Phallon Tullis-Joyce.

But United eventually got the goal their pressure deserved in the 72nd minute. Hanna Lundkvist sent the ball across the box and Julia Zigiotti Olme arrived at the back post to slot home the winner

Villa pushed for an equaliser, but United stood firm to take all three points.

articles.title: Al Ajax de Míchel se le escapa el liderato de la Eredivisie en el descuento
articles.standfirst: El Twente logró igualar un 0-2 con un penalti transformado por Weghorst
articles.summary: El Twente logró igualar un 0-2 con un penalti transformado por Weghorst
articles.body: Jornada 32 de la 24-25. Hasta ahí hay que remontarse para recuperar la última vez que el Ajax fue líder de la Eredivisie. Tras le derrota del Feyenoord ante el Heerenven (5-3), los de Míchel tenían en su manos marcharse al parón en lo más alto de la tabla. El Twente, sin embargo, se lo negó tras igualar un 0-2 en el descuento (2-2). Tolu Arokodare fue el encargado de comenzar a encarrilar la situación cuando todavía no habían transcurrido ni cinco minutos de partido. Recibió Gloukh en banda izquierda y envió un centro preciso al segundo palo que el ex del Wolverhampton cabeceó con contundencia. Enlaza cinco partidos consecutivos viendo portería en los que ha marcado seis goles. Mediada la segunda parte, el propio Gloukh sirvió su segunda asistencia de la tarde. Esta vez, en favor de un Rayane Bounida que transformó el 0-2 con un disparo lejano. No estuvo acertado Dommel. Un ex del Ajax como Weghorst recortó distancia sólo dos minutos después a la salida de un córner. Poco pudo hacer Ter Stegen. Parecía que le iba a tocar terminar sufriendo a un Ajax al que el VAR le negó un penalti a falta de un cuarto de hora para el final. Y es que, cuando ya se veían con el triunfo en el bolsillo, Lucas Rosa cometió un penalti sobre Zerrouki. Weghorst no tuvo piedad alguna y batió a Ter Stegen.

articles.summary: Mikautadze y Gueye son los máximo goleadores del Villarreal en Liga. Ambos llevan tres goles. Estos son los números de delantero georgiano en LaLiga e
articles.body:
Última hora del Villarreal - Getafe, en directo

Muy buenas tardes a todos. Arrancamos con la narración en directo del partido Villarreal - Getafe, correspondiente a la jornada 12 de LaLiga EA Sports . Un encuentro que entre dos equipo que viven horas bajas y en el que se juegan mucho.

El Villarreal afronta el duelo tras la goleada recibida en Champions League a manos del PSG de Luis Enrique (0-6), que ha hecho que aparezcan dudas sobre la viabilidad del proyecto deportivo que encabeza Iñigo Pérez. No solo por el abultado resultado recibido frente al cuadro francés, sino también por la trayectoria del equipo en lo que va de temporada, lejos de los puestos de cabeza en Liga (12 puntos, los mismos que el Getafe, su rival de hoy) y fuera de top 24 en la Champions. No sería descabellado pensar que la propiedad pudiera tomar medidas, si hoy se produce un nuevo descalabro.

Para este encuentro, Iñigo Pérez no podrá contar con Ilias, Foyth, Gerard Moreno y Diatta, todo ellos lesionados. Precisamente Diatta pasó por el quirófano el pasado jueves , por una lesión en la musculatura isquiotibial, y estará de baja medio año.

La situación del Getafe tampoco es idílica . El equipo de Bordalás viene de perder en la Conference League frente al Brighton. Mientras que ganó el último partido liguero disputado ante el Sevilla. El reto para el conjunto getafense es lograr su primera victoria fuera de casa esta temporada, algo que se les resiste a los azulones. El técnico tiene las bajas de Juanmi y Uche.

El partido arranca a las 18.30 horas en el estado de La Cerámica y será dirigido por el colegiado aragonés Carlos Muñiz . En el VAR estará Valentín Pizarro . Queda presentado el partido. Desde ya os vamos a ir contando todas las novedades que se produzcan en torno a este atractivo encuentro. Comenzamos.

articles.title: Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool: Pierre Sage in big trouble as Eagles hit rock-bottom in Premier League
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as goals from Alexis Mac Allister, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak help Liverpool return to winning ways after back-to-back defeats, piling the pressure on Crystal Palace head coach Pierre Sage heading into the international break
articles.body:
Palace substitute Eddie Nketiah pulled a goal back from the spot with the last kick of the game, but the damage was already done after Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz struck for Liverpool either side of half time and Alexander Isak added a third late on.

Liverpool secured a much-needed result following back-to-back defeats at Arsenal and Fenerbahce. The victory, their first for three games in all competitions, moves Liverpool up to fourth in the table.

Goalkeeper Alisson Becker, arguably Liverpool's best player, kept his side in the game, producing important saves to keep out Daichi Kamada and Adam Wharton in a first half that also saw Palace hit the bar through Yeremy Pino. He finished with six saves.

Palace's hard work was undone by Quinten Timber losing Mac Allister at a free-kick five minutes before the break, allowing the Argentina international to head in his fifth goal of the season - as many as he managed in the entirety of last season.

Liverpool's two £100m players then combined to double their lead as Bradley Barcola found Wirtz after a swift counter-attack. The Germany international picked out the corner to score his first league goal of the season after a 12-game barren run in the competition.

With the game already sealed, Isak compounded Sage's misery by adding a third in the 89th minute before Palace scored from the spot deep in stoppage-time after Milos Kerkez was judged to have fouled fellow substitute Dario Osorio in the box.

Nketiah's spot-kick prevented Sage from becoming the first Palace head coach since Frank de Boer to lose four games in a row without scoring. Nonetheless, Sage looks set for the same fate as De Boer, who was sacked after his fourth defeat in that run.

"I think that would have been one of the best Crystal Palace performances this season. Liverpool won 3-1 away from home but their goalkeeper was their best player. That tells you how well Palace did.

"But I don't think you can hang your hat on the performance, especially with a new guy into the Premier League. He's really struggled so far.

"I don't think you can take the risk as an owner when you think of the finances involved. Palace - 14 seasons in the Premier League, we don't expect them to be [bottom]. They're an established Premier League club.

"I think the decision will be made, unfortunately for Pierre Sage. I think Palace will have a new manager the next time they play in the Premier League"

18: OFF THE BAR! Pino goes agonisingly close to giving Palace the lead

32: GOAL DISALLOWED! Strand Larsen finds the back of the net but had strayed offside

37: BIG MISS! Barcola fires well over the bar from close-range on the volley

38: SAVE! Kamada's volleyed effort is saved by Liverpool 'keeper Alisson

40: GOAL! Mac Allister heads Liverpool from Szoboszlai's free-kick after losing his marker Timber

43: SAVE! Alisson produces another important save to keep out Wharton's glancing header

54: GOAL! Wirtz converts from Barcola's cross to double Liverpool's lead from swift counter

77: SAVE! Alisson to the rescue again as he produces a double save to keep out Pino and Lerma

89: GOAL! Isak's deflected strike seals the win for Liverpool in south London.

90+5: GOAL! Nketiah scores from the spot with final kick of the game after Osorio was fouled by Kerkez

Crystal Palace have conceded 24 Premier League goals this season, their most in their first 10 matches of any league campaign since 1980-81 (also 24).

Only Chelsea (8) have conceded more goals from non-penalty set-pieces in the Premier League this season than Crystal Palace (6).

Liverpool have earned more points away from home in the Premier League this season than any other side (13). It's the Reds' joint-most ever from their first five away matches of a league campaign.

articles.title: El Liverpool se levanta... y deja herido al Crystal Palace
articles.standfirst: Goleada para dejar atrás las derrotas ante Arsenal y Fenerbahçe
articles.summary: Goleada para dejar atrás las derrotas ante Arsenal y Fenerbahçe
articles.body: Las derrotas contra Arsenal y Fenerbahçe habían puesto fin a una racha de cinco victorias consecutivas por parte del Liverpool. Los de Iraola, sin embargo, lograron reponerse antes del parón de selecciones goleando al Crystal Palace (1-3) en Shelhurts Park gracias a los goles de Mac Allister, Wirtz e Isak. A pesar de los últimos resultados, fue sorprendente que Iraola sacase del once a un Trey Nyoni que ha derribado la puerta. Fue Szoboszlai quien recuperó su puesto en la medular junto a Mac Allister. También regresaron Araújo, Kerkez, Wirtz, Gakpo e Isak tras descansar en Estambul. Yéremy Pino, como suele ser habitual, fue titular en la doble mediapunta del Palace, mientras que Mingueza apareció en el carril derecho. No había transcurrido ni un minuto de partido y Dean Henderson ya se había embolsado un lanzamiento lejano a cargo de Mac Allister para quitarse el mal sabor de boca de no haber probado a Raya la semana pasada. Dejó claro el Liverpool que su intención pasaba por imprimirle ritmo al choque desde el inicio. Se instalaron en campo rival y, sobre todo, apretaron cada reinicio del Palace. Trató de ganar protagonismo Wirtz desde la mediapunta... aunque fue Szoboszlai quien más comenzó a producir desde su golpeo. Henderson le sacó a córner un 'latigazo' lejano con la zurda y, acto seguido, sirvió un centro lateral que Gakpo no logró dirigir entre palos en el segundo palo. La tuvo todavía más clara Pino mandando un 'zurdazo' al larguero tras recibir completamente solo en el interior del área. Se animó el Crystal Palace y, nada más cumplirse la primera media hora de encuentro, Strand Larsen vio cómo le anulaban el posible 1-0 por fuera de juego. También apareció Alisson para salvar un 'voleón' de Kamada a 'bocajarro'. Tres avisos lo suficientemente serios para un Liverpool que, cuando parecía tambalearse, logró ponerse en ventaja a cinco minutos del descanso. Szoboszlai sirvió una falta lateral bien tocada que Mac Allister cabeceó en el primer palo. Entró con energía el Crystal Palace a la segunda mitad. Sin embargo, el cambio de banda de Gakpo y Barcola por parte de Iraola no tardó en dar sus frutos para el Liverpool. Araújo puso a correr al francés por derecha y puso un envío al área para la llegada desde segunda línea por parte de un Florian Wirtz que definió con sutileza. Dio un pequeño paso atrás el Liverpool y, con la entrada de Nyoni, Victor Muñoz y y Ngumoha, trataron de terminar de resolver el partido saliendo a la contra. A falta de 15' para el final, Pino no logró resolver un mano a mano ante Alisson que hubiese metido en el partido a un Crystal Palace que cerró la jornada como colista de la Premier. Isak hizo el 0-3 al filo del descuento... aunque Nketiah maquilló el marcador de penalti en la última jugada.

articles.title: Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea: Enzo Le Fee's penalty lifts Black Cats off bottom of table as Xabi Alonso's side show more inconsistency
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Chelsea were beaten 1-0 by bottom club Sunderland; Brian Brobbey won a penalty off Levi Colwill which Enzo Le Fee converted; Chelsea were second best and failed to create many chances of note, despite trailing; Cole Palmer was denied a first-half penalty
articles.body:
Xabi Alonso's side were second-best throughout. None of their midfield attack won a duel or a tackle in the opening 20 minutes, while Sunderland's fight was best shown through Brian Brobbey's efforts up front.

The Dutch international smashed his way through Chelsea centre-backs Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill in a brutal first half - coming close to scoring twice, before eventually getting his rewards.

Ten minutes before half-time, he rolled past Colwill with immense strength to win a penalty, which Enzo Le Fee converted. Colwill was then taken off at half-time.

If Chelsea were weak in defence, they weren't much better in attack. They struggled to break down a Sunderland defence that has been leaking goals of late. Morgan Rogers went closest in the first half with an off-target header, while their only chance of note in the second half was Danny Welbeck's injury-time miss.

Chelsea had a penalty shout in the first half when the mostly-ineffective Cole Palmer burst through and went down under two Sunderland challenges right on the edge of the penalty area - but VAR controversially said there was no foul regardless of whether it was inside or outside the box.

Sunderland were still the better team throughout - despite losing captain Granit Xhaka after three minutes due to injury - and looked more likely to get a second goal than Chelsea were to getting an equaliser. Substitute Wilson Isidor nearly made it 2-0 when he was one-on-one but Mike Penders denied him in style.

The result moves Sunderland off the bottom of the table, while Chelsea have lost their place in the top four as their inconsistency continues.

3: INJURY! Sunderland are dealt an early blow as Xhaka limps off after going down off the ball.

14: BIG MISS! Chesmine Talbi starts the game strongly, curling in a cross which Brobbey fails to convert.

24: NO PENALTY! Palmer goes down under a double challenge from Luke O'Nien and substitute Jules Ahoka right on the line of the penalty area. But VAR says no foul when checking it.

25: BIG MISS! Rogers heads Marco Palestra's cross off target after leaping well in the penalty area.

28: CHANCE! Brobbey takes on last defender Fofana but his touch takes him wide and he shoots off target.

36: GOAL! Brobbey's hard work eventually comes off as he grapples with Colwill to win a penalty, which Le Fee converts.

61: BIG TACKLE! Estevao comes on at half-time and Rogers tries to poke the ball through to him but Thomas Meunier comes up with a goal-saving tackle.

77: BIG SAVE! A loose ball breaks to Isidor but his powerful effort when through on goal is saved by Penders.

81: WIDE! Chelsea's first chance of note in the second half sees Geovany Quenda fire wide of the far post.

90+2: OVER! Welbeck heads over Estevao's free-kick from inside the box.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso to Sky Sports:

"We were missing a bit of speed on the ball, a bit of patience playing against a low block.

"We didn't create enough chances, we didn't have enough patience or creativity to create chances. That's why we were not close to scoring.

"We could have done even better. We didn't do enough to score what would have been the equaliser."

On Palmer's penalty shout: "I haven't seen Cole's actions, but there could be a chance that it could be given."

On the Sunderland penalty: "The other one, I think it's an action where he can defend better. It's our mistake."

Le Bris: The connection with fans was perfect

Sunderland head coach Regis Le Bris to Sky Sports:

"It's not an easy task because the schedule is so tough, every three days you have to reset and go again with different starting elevens. But today, the connection was perfect.

"Sunderland is unique for that point. When I first came in, I was really surprised how connected our fanbase is connected with our identity of the club and the game model. The more we play this style of play, the more the supporters settle which helps the energy to grow in the stadium. It supports the players.

"We have to play on the edge. Football is like that, you're walking on a tightrope and can have problems sometimes.

"The depth of the squad is important. The Europa League and Carabao Cup helped, we played with many young players. The performance wasn't always great but we're talking about experiences. The combined experiences, you have to play different game. Jules [Ahoka] was impressive this afternoon.

"We need good players on the pitch. Brian is one of them. The strikers are rare, we have one really good striker. He trusts the club, the identity of the region. He showed this afternoon that he can fight until the end."

articles.title: Ipswich 1-2 Bournemouth: Evanilson scores again as Cherries make it eight wins in a row
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Bournemouth record an eighth straight win in all competitions and their fourth in the Premier League; Evanilson took advantage of a shocking error from Christian Walton to send them on their way
articles.body:
Evanilson scored for the fifth Premier League game running when taking advantage of a shocking error from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton, who tried to dribble around the striker.

Bournemouth arrived in Suffolk eager to complete an almost perfect month since the last international break with another three points and Alex Scott returned to the bench in another boost for Marco Rose.

Ipswich started the second half in nightmare fashion in a very sloppy overall performance, with the Cherries given a helping hand to score again after 27 seconds.

Abdoul Ouattara was initially at fault by giving the ball away to Evanilson and, after possession was moved on to Christie, the Bournemouth midfielder's rising strike deflected off first Issa Diop and then the chest of Ipswich left-back Leif Davis on its way in.

Ipswich hadn't registered a shot or even a touch in the Bournemouth box in the second half until Jack Clarke scored from the penalty spot with 13 minutes remaining.

Fatigue and nerves started to creep in late on for Bournemouth, who had to stand strong in nine minutes of injury time.

Julio Enciso threatened from distance but Marco Rose's side head into the international break in seventh place, just three points off the top four.

articles.title: Brighton 2-0 Brentford: Diego Gomez scores thunderbolt as Seagulls enter November international break in second
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Premier League match between Brighton and Brentford at the Amex; goals from Diego Gomez and Pascal Gross send Fabian Hurzeler's Seagulls up to second; Bees striker Igor Thiago shown straight red card for an arm in the face of Chema
articles.body:
The job was done for the Seagulls by the break, with Diego Gomez and Pascal Gross scoring either side of the straight red card shown to Bees striker Igor Thiago after he caught Chema in the face with his arm and split his lip.

As a result, Fabian Hurzeler's side enter the November international break five points behind league leaders Arsenal.

Brighton took the lead after 15 minutes in stunning fashion. Gomez seized on a poor defensive header and arrowed an unstoppable strike - worthy of all superlatives - high into the top-left corner.

And the outlook improved significantly for the hosts less than 10 minutes later, when Thiago was given his marching orders after referee Michael Oliver's brief visit to the VAR monitor to overturn his original decision to show the Brazilian only a yellow.

It was attack vs defence thereafter, with Brighton putting Brentford under heavy pressure. They got their reward when they were given a penalty after Keane Lewis-Potter dragged Luka Vuskovic to the deck as a corner was delivered from the right.

The execution from Gross was near-perfect; a thumping penalty into the postage stamp that Caoimhin Kelleher had no chance of stopping.

Brighton's comfort in the game was never in doubt after the break. They had almost 80 per cent possession and various chances - though there was little of quality, on the whole.

By then the wind had long been taken from the sails of Brentford, whose 200th Premier League game ended in misery.

articles.title: Barcelona register interest in signing €80 million-rated Chelsea defender – report
articles.summary: It is no secret that Barcelona are in dire need of reinforcements in the defensive department, having been dealt multiple injury blows in the past month or s...
articles.body:
It is no secret that Barcelona are in dire need of reinforcements in the defensive department, having been dealt multiple injury blows in the past month or so.

Signing a new central defender could be a priority for Barcelona in the upcoming January transfer window.

The club have already been linked with multiple centre-backs heading into January and it appears there is a latest entrant on the list.

Colwill has been a regular under Xabi Alonso at Chelsea. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images)

As reported by Mundo Deportivo , Barcelona have registered interest in Chelsea defender Levi Colwill ahead of the January transfer window.

A product of the Chelsea youth academy, Colwill is regarded highly in the Blues setup and has seen rapid growth in the past couple of years, especially after a loan spell at Brighton & Hove Albion.

A left-footed centre-back with exceptional ball-playing qualities, Colwill has become a starter under Xabi Alonso at Chelsea this season.

The Englishman's performances have not gone unnoticed, with Barcelona among the clubs interested in his services, as they look to shore up their defensive unit.

All eyes on Colwill's future. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

However, acquiring the services of Colwill won't be a walk in the park for Barcelona.

For one, the defender has a contract at Stamford Bridge until 2029, thus giving Chelsea some key leverage in negotiations.

Moreover, the Blues want to extend the contract, which could further raise his current price tag of around €80 million, which itself is a challenge for Barcelona.

There is hope that interest from Barça and Liverpool could sway Colwill into stalling negotiations with Chelsea, but coach Xabi Alonso has no desire to part ways with the defender.

Chelsea, for their part, will not entertain any offers below their €80 million price-tag, thus making Colwill a costly target for the Catalans, at least under the current economic circumstances.

Barcelona, therefore, may end up looking at other options, with the club notably being linked with a move for Manchester United star Lisandro Martinez , among others.

articles.title: Making perfect sense of four two-loss football teams in SEC Power Rankings
articles.summary: Texas, Alabama, Kentucky and Tennessee have all lost twice. How did they shake out in the SEC Power Rankings? We make sense of it here.
articles.body:
Week 10 in the SEC was sure to be a bloody one, with the top eight teams in the league clashing amongst each other in four games. When the dust settled, LSU, Ole Miss and Missouri found themselves on the wrong side of the College Football Playoff, and hoping for chaos the rest of the season. Onto the rankings!

What to know : After a 42-7 win at Ole Miss, something tells us the Bulldogs hadn't forgotten who knocked them out of the CFP in January.

What to know : Texas 34, Refs 1, Missouri 20.

What to know : The Vols' jump forward in the CFP standings this week is going to look like Evel Knievel clearing 14 Greyhound buses in 1975 .

What to know : If Lane Kiffin thought Nick Saban was the reason he couldn't beat Alabama, Kalen DeBoer showed him otherwise.

What to know : The Will Stein Experience has been quite a ride, but Tennessee didn't buy a ticket for it.

What to know : Your father's Ole Miss showed up for the Georgia game.

What to know : Against Alabama , he's Lane Whiffin'

What to know : That 24-team playoff can't come fast enough for Eli Drinkwitz.

What to know : Make it four wins in a row for the Gamecocks, and Shane Beamer's chair is back to a low simmer.

What to know : Proposed trade − Ole Miss shows OU how to score, Sooners show the Rebels how to tackle.

What to know : Oklahoma bent the Gators defense, then broke it, on a 20-play, 89-yard drive that took 12:45 off the clock.

What to know : If it takes a little Jordan-Hare magic to nip Arkansas, the Tigers need a new trick.

What to know : The Commodores handed keys to the cellar to Arkansas, but they've still got the master key.

What to know : MSU without Kamario Taylor is worse than Popeye without spinach.

articles.title: Kickoff time, TV network, odds announced for Arizona football’s game vs. Utah
articles.summary: Arizona football will get a primetime billing for one of its biggest home games in years. Arizona and Utah will kick off at 5:30 p.m. MST at Casino Del Stadi...
articles.body:
Arizona football will get a primetime billing for one of its biggest home games in years.

Arizona and Utah will kick off at 5:30 p.m. MST at Casino Del Stadium, and the game will be televised on Fox, the Big 12 announced Sunday.

Utah has opened as a 2.5-point favorite, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under is 53.5 points.

Arizona (7-2) needs a win over Utah in order to keep its Big 12 title game and College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Utes are coming off a rivalry victory over BYU that moved Morgan Scalley 's team to 9-0 on the season.

Arizona is hosting a top-3 team for the first time since 2007 , when No. 2 Oregon came to town — a game Arizona won in dramatic fashion.

The small spread suggests oddsmakers believe Arizona can pull off a similar upset this Saturday.

Arizona is just 3-6 against the spread (ATS) this season, with two of the three covers coming at home. The Wildcats failed to cover on Friday, hanging on to beat TCU 29-28 in a game they were favored to win by a touchdown.

Brent Brennan 's squad has won seven consecutive games at Casino Del Stadium, with the last loss coming in 2025 against No. 18 BYU.

Arizona is 6-7 against Utah since the Utes joined the Pac-12 in 2011. All-time, the Utes have a 26-21 lead in the series.

Brennan's highest ranked win at Arizona was at Utah in 2024, when the Wildcats upset the No. 10 ranked Utes. Arizona won the previous meeting between the two schools in Tucson in 2023. Arizona and Utah didn't play each other last year.

This Utah team relies on an highly efficient offense that Arizona fans were unaccustomed to seeing in the Kyle Whittingham era. Utah ranks 13th nationally with 37.7 points per game and 12th with 215 rushing yards.

Utah is 8-1 ATS. The lone game Utah didn't cover was a 27-24 victory at Colorado.

Utah quarterback Devon Dampier , a Phoenix native, has 2,053 passing yards including 20 touchdowns and seven interceptions. He has another 480 yards on the ground including seven rushing scores.

articles.title: Napoli hold Serie A leaders Lazio, Milan cast aside Euro blues at Genoa
articles.summary: Serie A leaders Lazio dropped points for just the second time this season in Sunday's 1-1 draw away to struggling Napoli, while AC Milan climbed into the top...
articles.body:
Serie A leaders Lazio dropped points for just the second time this season in Sunday's 1-1 draw away to struggling Napoli, while AC Milan climbed into the top four with a 2-1 win at Genoa.

Davide Frattesi gave the Romans a deserved lead but Napoli drew level early in the second half through an Alfonso Pedraza own goal.

Napoli were under pressure to deliver a result after defeats by Juventus and Porto saw the squad sent into a training retreat in a bid to revive their flagging form.

But they could only claim a point against Gennaro Gattuso's unbeaten outfit, whose remarkable form continued as they moved two points clear on top on 29 points, 14 ahead of Napoli in 10th place.

"We must keep going, everything's not lost even if we are behind in the standings," Napoli head coach Massimiliano Allegri told DAZN.

"We are not out of the race for the top four, the Coppa Italia or the Champions League. There are difficult moments over the course of a season, and they must be faced calmly."

The visitors, targeting a seventh league win in a row and fifth consecutive away victory in Naples, started strongly as Gustav Isaksen and Josip Sutalo drew diving saves from Vanja Milinkovic-Savic.

The Romans went in front in the 28th minute when Frattesi raced on to Tijjani Noslin's through ball and finished emphatically for his fourth goal of the season.

Lazio's opener sparked a reaction from Napoli as Christos Mandas denied Rasmus Hojlund before half-time substitute Pedraza inadvertently turned a cross into his own net early in the second half.

The hosts came closest to a winner as Scott McTominay tested Mandas with a low shot before Kevin De Bruyne saw a shot charged down by the Greek goalkeeper and the rebound cleared off the line by Reda Belahyane.

Milan moved above Como into fourth as Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic struck in a 2-1 victory.

Ruben Amorim's team finished a mixed week on a high with a second Serie A win on the bounce.

Milan claimed a memorable derby win over rivals Inter Milan last weekend, but inconsistency reared its head again with a 2-0 Europa League loss at home to Ferencvaros on Thursday.

Amorim was left furious by his side's performance in that game but saw a much improved start from his players at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris.

Cisse swept in the opener after 13 minutes for his fifth league goal of the season, before Pulisic took advantage of a defensive mix-up to double their lead six minutes later.

Mikael Ellertsson pulled one back for Genoa late on with a deflected strike from range.

Milan have alternated wins and defeats for the last seven games in all competitions but have 24 points, five fewer than leaders Lazio.

Atalanta ended a six-match winless run in all competitions by beating Monza 1-0 thanks to a Nikola Krstovic strike.

Champions Inter Milan will move one point behind Lazio if they beat Como later on Sunday, before Fiorentina host Juventus.

articles.title: El Milan no le pierde la cara al Scudetto
articles.standfirst: Los tempraneros goles de Cissè y Pulisic solventan el triunfo frente al Genoa
articles.summary: Los tempraneros goles de Cissè y Pulisic solventan el triunfo frente al Genoa
articles.body: La joven promesa milanista Alphadjo Cisse celebró este domingo con un gol que abrió el marcador ante el Génova la noticia de su primera convocatoria con Italia, en un encuentro que el Milan terminó ganando por 1-2 gracias a otro tanto de Christian Pulisic. El equipo milanés, que mira a los primeros puestos, se colocó con este importante triunfo cuarto en la clasificación, a un punto del tercero, el Inter, y del quinto, el Como, que se enfrentan entre ellos este domingo. Los 'rossoneri' frenaron, además, la racha victoriosa del Génova, que había encadenado tres victorias consecutivas. El equipo del norte de Italia abrió la lata pronto, en el minuto 13, cuando Cisse, que vive una semana feliz tras ser convocado por primera vez con la 'Azzurra', remató solo, tras desmarcarse de forma inteligente, desde la frontal para batir a Justin Bijlow y sellar su cuarto gol en liga tras el doblete al Bolonia y otro tanto al Torino. El segundo llegó seis minutos después, en el 19, después de otra pérdida del Génova en la construcción. Traoré intentó jugar en horizontal hacia Ostigard, pero Gonçalo Ramos interceptó el pase, se internó en el área y asistió a Pulisic, que cruzó el balón con la derecha para ampliar la ventaja. El equipo genovés trató de reaccionar y llegó a celebrar un tanto de Milutin Osmajic en el minuto 30, pero el árbitro lo anuló por un fuera de juego milimétrico, confirmado tras la revisión del VAR. Tras la reanudación, el Génova adelantó sus líneas y aumentó la presión en busca de un gol que le permitiera regresar al encuentro, si bien el Milan, por su parte, optó por proteger su ventaja y buscar salidas rápidas. Luka Modric, como líder del centro del campo, controló el partido y Pulisic ejerció como el más peligroso del conjunto visitante. La segunda parte estuvo marcada también por la tensión en los banquillos. Tres integrantes de la expedición milanista, dos ayudantes del técnico y el médico, fueron expulsados por sus protestas. Empató el Génova en el 87 por medio de Mikael Egill Ellertsson, pero era demasiado tarde. El Milan fue capaz de amarrar tres puntos fundamentales en su lucha para no descolgarse y para coger confianza, después del tropiezo en casa contra el Ferencvaros en Liga Europa del pasado jueves. El duelo entre 'Il Grifone', denominado así por la criatura mitológica emblema de Génova desde época medieval, y 'Los Diablos', supuso el primer enfrentamiento entre Daniele de Rossi y Rúben Amorim, líderes de dos de los clubes pioneros de la Serie A.

articles.title: Garcia, Schick take Leverkusen to derby win at Cologne
articles.summary: Goals from Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick took Bayer Leverkusen to a tense 2-1 derby win at Cologne on Sunday, lifting the visitors to fifth in the Bundeslig...
articles.body:
Goals from Aleix Garcia and Patrik Schick took Bayer Leverkusen to a tense 2-1 derby win at Cologne on Sunday, lifting the visitors to fifth in the Bundesliga table.

Garcia curled an excellent effort into the top corner after just seven minutes and Schick scored five minutes from time in a fiery encounter which produced 11 yellow cards, including six for the hosts.

Germany starlet Said El Mala scored a stoppage-time consolation goal for the hosts, who sit in 15th spot, just one clear of the relegation playoff placing.

One of several derbies in Germany's football-mad north-west, Cologne and Leverkusen are just 10 kilometres (six miles) apart.

The travelling support teased the hosts with chants referring to the 2023-24 season, when Leverkusen won their maiden Bundesliga title and Cologne were relegated.

Leverkusen broke through just seven minutes in when Garcia's free-kick flew over the wall and into the top-left corner, with a helpless Cologne goalie Marvin Schwaebe watching on.

Just before the break, the Spaniard found Jarell Quansah in space but the England centre-back headed just wide.

Well handled by the Leverkusen defence, the hosts grew increasingly frustrated, picking up five of their six yellow cards in the second-half.

Schick had a goal rubbed out for handball with ten minutes to go but broke through just five minutes later, slotting in on the counter for an eighth goal in nine league games this season.

El Mala scored one of his own in stoppage time but the goal came too late to launch a Cologne comeback.

Later on Sunday, Freiburg can climb to third spot with a win at home over strugglers Union Berlin, while Hoffenheim host promoted Schalke.
